I volunteer at the local animal shelter once a month to socialize the shy cats.
I vividly remember the power going out during a blizzard and reading by candlelight.
I went to a concert by myself last year and was surprised by how much fun I had.
I hate the sound of people chewing, which makes team lunches at work unbearable.
I secretly love listening to boy band music from the early 2000s when I clean my apartment.
I remember the relief of paying off my car loan after five years of monthly installments.
I get extremely anxious whenever I have to make small talk with my company CEO in the elevator.
I broke my toe by stubbing it on my coffee table in the middle of the night.
I tried knitting again recently but immediately remembered why I gave it up in middle school.
I once overheard a coworker making a snide comment about my lunches, which made me cry in the bathroom.
I love the feeling of climbing into bed with freshly washed sheets.
I have a favorite mug with a chipped handle that I refuse to throw away.
I went to a speed dating event and ended up just talking to the bartender all night.
I always double-check that my front door is locked at least three times before going to sleep.
I remember the thrill of finding a vintage designer jacket at a thrift store for five dollars.
I had a terrible bout of food poisoning after eating gas station sushi on a road trip.
I cried during a musical performance because the music was so overwhelmingly beautiful.
I have a recurring dream where I am back in college and forgot to attend a class all semester.
I got stuck in a horrible traffic jam for four hours and had to pee on the side of the highway.
I love going to the farmers market on Saturday mornings just to look at the fresh flowers.
I remember my childhood bedroom had glow-in-the-dark stars on the ceiling that I put up myself.

After my quick checkup in January ended with a generic lecture about cutting carbs, I walked out of the office feeling entirely abandoned by the medical system. I ended up spending my entire weekend researching macro-tracking apps because I had to manage my obesity completely on my own.
I used to pretend I was sick so I could stay home from school and watch game shows.
I was caught passing a note in fifth grade and had to read it aloud to the class.
My high school boyfriend dumped me the week before prom, leaving me without a date.
I remember sneaking out of my house once just to sit on the roof and look at the neighborhood.
I took a photography class in college and spent hours developing film in the darkroom.
I completely blanked during a presentation in my senior seminar and stood in silence for a full minute.
I love baking banana bread on Sunday afternoons when the weather is gloomy.
I got a speeding ticket on my way to work and was in a terrible mood for the rest of the week.
I always order exactly the same drink at the coffee shop because I fear I will not like a new one.

I was incredibly receptive when the nurse practitioner at Oak Street Health offered to send a direct referral to a structured commercial weight-management program. I signed the paperwork immediately in the exam room because having access to an established system sounded much better than guessing at my diet.
I had to fire an employee for the first time last month and it made me feel sick to my stomach.
I enjoy organizing my bookshelf by color even though it makes finding specific books harder.
I was stung by a bee at a company picnic and my eye swelled shut.
I remember the absolute terror of losing my wallet in a foreign city during a study abroad trip.
I always keep a pair of emergency flats under my desk in case my heels hurt too much.
I hate confrontation so much that I once let a hair stylist cut my hair way too short without complaining.
I look forward to my annual cabin trip with my college roommates every October.
I recently started taking a daily walk on my lunch break to get away from my computer screen.

The bariatric specialist I consulted gave me a highly specific protein-cycling schedule that perfectly accommodated my demanding full-time corporate job. In contrast, my regular primary care doctor previously just told me to exercise more, completely lacking the actionable guidance I received from the specialist.
I felt incredibly validated when my manager praised my conflict-resolution skills during my performance review.
I have a scar on my chin from tripping over a vacuum cord when I was a toddler.
I remember the frustration of trying to assemble furniture by myself and putting a piece on backwards.
I often avoid looking in full-length mirrors on days when my body image is particularly bad.
I got a terrible sunburn on my scalp because I forgot to wear a hat at a baseball game.
I love the crisp smell of autumn air and the crunch of leaves under my boots.
I won a fifty-dollar gift card at my office holiday party raffle last year.
I occasionally cancel plans at the last minute just because I want to stay home in my sweatpants.
I remember my mother teaching me how to make her famous lasagna recipe.
I was deeply embarrassed when my card was declined at the grocery store due to a bank error.
I always cry at weddings, even if I barely know the couple getting married.
I took a painting class and discovered that I am absolutely terrible at watercolors.
I have a specific music playlist for when I need to power through tedious spreadsheets at work.
I remember the joy of adopting a pair of guinea pigs when I was nine years old.
I got horribly lost in the subway system the first time I visited New York City.
I love the routine of making my coffee in the French press every morning.
I was surprisingly good at playing dodgeball in middle school because I could duck quickly.
I remember the distinct smell of chlorine from the public pool where I took swimming lessons.
I had braces for three years and absolutely hated the feeling of the tightening wire.
I always buy a new planner in January with grand intentions of staying organized, but abandon it by March.
I once choked on a piece of ice at a restaurant and everyone stared at me.
I found a stray kitten in my alley and spent three hours trying to catch it to take it to the shelter.
I remember the sting of being left out when my friends went to the mall without me in seventh grade.
I always check the weather app before leaving the house but rarely dress appropriately anyway.
I successfully changed a flat tire by myself on the side of a busy road.
I felt extremely awkward attending my ten-year high school reunion so I left early.
I keep a box of old birthday cards and letters under my bed because I cannot bear to throw them away.
I love watching cooking competition shows while eating microwave dinners.
I accidentally dropped my phone in the toilet and had to put it in a bag of rice for two days.
I remember the taste of the cheap pizza my friends and I would buy after Friday night football games.
I got dizzy and nearly fainted when I tried to donate blood in college.
I dread the company team-building exercises because they always involve forced vulnerability.
I have a favorite cozy sweater that is practically falling apart but I refuse to throw it away.
I remember the quiet peace of waking up early to watch the sunrise over the lake on a camping trip.
I completely ruined a silk shirt by throwing it in the washing machine with my towels.
I feel a sense of accomplishment every time I manage to keep my email inbox empty.
I hate making phone calls and will do anything to handle an issue via text instead.
I remember the sharp pain of stepping on a stray plastic block in my younger brother bedroom.
I got locked out of my apartment in my pajamas and had to ask my neighbor to borrow his phone.
I was so nervous for my driving test that I parallel parked perfectly out of pure adrenaline.
I have an irrational fear of riding escalators that are going down.
I once tripped walking up the stairs at graduation and felt like everyone in the auditorium saw me.
I love the feeling of finally taking my bra off at the end of a long workday.
I remember exactly where I was sitting when I heard the news that my parents were getting divorced.
I keep buying fresh spinach with the intention of making salads, but it always wilts in the fridge.
I had a crush on a barista and went to his coffee shop every day for a month just to see him.
I successfully assembled a massive jigsaw puzzle over the course of a snowy weekend.
I once tried to cut my own bangs in high school and had to wear headbands for months to hide the disaster.
I remember the comforting sound of my dad snoring echoing down the hallway when I was a kid.
I bought an expensive gym membership but I feel too intimidated by the equipment to actually go.
I always get the hiccups when I eat spicy food too quickly.
I found a twenty-dollar bill in the pocket of my winter coat when I unpacked it for the season.
I remember the sheer panic of realizing I had slept through my alarm on the morning of a final exam.
I love the smell of old books and frequently visit a local used bookstore just to browse.
I fell asleep on a bus and missed my stop, ending up in a completely unfamiliar neighborhood.
I sometimes pretend to be on my phone to avoid talking to people I recognize in the grocery store.
I felt an overwhelming sense of loneliness on my thirtieth birthday when I realized I was still single.
I always sing loudly in the shower when I know my neighbors are not home.
I remember the metallic taste of blood in my mouth after getting my wisdom teeth removed.
I have a terrible habit of biting my nails whenever I am stressed about a deadline at work.
I tried to bake macarons from scratch and they turned into a flat, sticky mess.
I was incredibly moved by a documentary about ocean conservation and immediately donated to a charity.
I once got caught in a sudden downpour on my way to an interview and arrived soaking wet.
I remember the comforting weight of the lead apron at the dentist office when getting x-rays.
I have a mild allergy to cats, but I take medicine every day because I love Barnaby too much.
I got a severe leg cramp in the middle of the night and woke up screaming.
I love the ritual of painting my nails every Sunday evening to prepare for the week ahead.
I felt completely unequipped to handle my friend grief when she lost her mother.
I remember the thrill of sneaking into a restricted movie with my friends when we were fifteen.
I always peel the crusts off my sandwiches, a habit I never grew out of from childhood.
I was surprisingly calm when my car slid on the icy highway, steering out of it safely.
I have an extensive collection of teas but almost always reach for peppermint.
I remember the disappointment of waking up on Christmas morning to find out it had not snowed.
I accidentally liked an old photo on my ex-boyfriend social media page and considered deleting my account.
I always keep a spare umbrella in the trunk of my car just in case.
I felt a profound sense of peace while sitting on a park bench watching the sunset last week.
